note: The semantic role layer. The contract has a palette, a surface layer and a
set of roles stated in prose; what it did not have was the binding between
them, so a consumer had to choose a colour for every role for itself.
That is not a small gap. It is why gnu6.live carries about two hundred and
fifty hardcoded hex values in one stylesheet: with no role to name, every
surface in the product had to pick a colour by hand, and a change of
substrate had to be redone by hand too.
A role is what a thing is for, not what it looks like. The light and the
dark substrate each bind the role to a token; the components then name the
The binding is the contract's. Which CSS custom property or Rust constant
carries the role is the target's.

surface-raised.meaning: A thing that sits on the page: a card, a panel, a tile.

surface-overlay.meaning: A thing that sits on top of a raised surface: a dialog, a menu, a popover.

surface-sunken.meaning: A well: a code block, a track, an inset that the page sits inside.

ink.meaning: The text a reader is expected to read first.

ink-muted.meaning: Text that supports the reading text and is not read first: a caption, a secondary label.

hairline.meaning: The line between two surfaces. Never a divider drawn in a colour of its own.

accent.meaning: The one colour the system spends. It marks the principal operation, and it is spent on nothing else.

accent-ink.meaning: The text that sits on the accent.

focus.meaning: The ring that says where the keyboard is. It is a graphic and not a text colour: the royal blue measures 4.85 against white and 3.68 against the dark surface, and it marks a ring, a line or an edge, and it never carries a sentence.

selection.meaning: The ground of a chosen thing. The choice is carried by a surface and by the accessible state, never by a hue alone.

info.meaning: The colour of an information: what a reader is told, as distinct from what they can act on. It is a deliberate tint and not a step of the royal blue, because the field uses it for information and not for identity or focus. It is a graphic colour and not a text colour, and it never carries a sentence. On the light substrate it wears the deeper tint, which measures 5.31 against white and 4.36 against the light surface, where the tint that serves the dark substrate would measure 2.94 and would not be seen. It is excluded from the sunken light surface, where it would not be seen either.

positive.meaning: A condition that is observed and is well, carried as a mark: a pip, a dot, an edge. It is never a background behind body text, because the approved green measures 4.52 against white and 3.72 against the light surface and would not read. It is excluded from the sunken light surface, where it measures less than three and would not be seen.

positive-surface.meaning: A tinted surface that carries the text of a condition that is well.

caution.meaning: A condition that is observed and asks for attention. On the light substrate it wears the darker step of its family — the amber measures 2.04 against white and would not read — and the darker step measures 6.16, so a sentence of caution can be written in it.

critical.meaning: A condition that is observed and is a failure. On the light substrate it wears the darker step of its family — the red measures 3.91 against white and would not read — and the darker step measures 7.49, so a sentence of failure can be written in it.

light.meaning: The light substrate. The system is light-first: the shell is the light one.
